lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | Aug 2022 - Jul 2024
- Owned the diagnostics service's monitoring dashboards across two major releases and the on-call rotation that used them.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases, adding automated regression checks that shortened release cycles from 2 weeks to 3 days.

- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue while rewriting the shared logging library, onboarding two new hires and taking over the weekend on-call rotation, which removed the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
- Raised diagnostic accuracy on 1,200 held-out cases from 71% to 79% by fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Cut p95 latency of single-request edge inference by 40% by serving the INT8 engine with dynamic batching.
- Using grouped tool-use rollouts, a composite reward over accuracy, citation validity and call count, and a GRPO loop with a frozen SFT reference, reduced end-to-end latency 5%.
- Stabilised GRPO training on sparse rewards by sampling a single rollout per prompt, so each update used exactly one scored trajectory.
- Documented the triage branch's abstention rules and escalation paths for the on-call reviewers, who adopted them as the team's runbook.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Cut p95 tool-call latency from 900 ms to 600 ms, a 50% reduction, by caching tool results and reusing completed sub-agent answers.
- Raised the runtime's task-completion rate by 12% on the benchmark suite, from 71% to 83%, by retrying failed sub-agent calls with their partial context.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Upstreamed 8 citation and faithfulness metrics to an open-source research-agent framework, where they now run in the default benchmark for every release.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Traced 3 structural pipeline defects in stability, sourcing and parameter handling to their modules with layered instrumentation; each was fixed upstream.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation, Kubernetes

items.says: Check that the code link leads to a polished, relevant, active profile.
items.because: An inactive or sparse link would not strengthen the application.

items.says: Make the date format consistent with the rest of the résumé.
Consider adding relevant coursework or a strong GPA.
Consider adding GPA if it is a selling point.
items.because: It may help for early-career roles.

items.says: Put the Mobility Systems internship before the Eastern Robotics job.
items.because: Reverse-chronological order makes the more recent experience easier to find.

items.says: Confirm that the job title is the official title.
Make the location formatting match the internship entry.
Clarify whether you owned the dashboards, the on-call rotation, or both.
items.because: Their relationship is hard to parse.

items.says: Make the accomplishment more concrete.
Say whether the latency figures came from production or load testing, and give relevant measurement conditions.
Distinguish the build threshold from the achieved p95 result.
Explain how the release-cycle duration was measured.
items.because: It would help readers judge the size of your contribution.

items.says: Clarify how directly the regression checks caused the shorter release cycle.
items.because: It would help readers judge the size of your contribution.

items.says: Split or prioritize the many accomplishments in this bullet.
items.because: The technical change and its outcome get buried.

items.says: Quantify the backlog improvement if you have a reliable figure.
Explain what “diagnostics triage branch” means to an outside reader.
Define the backlog comparison, including its starting point and measurement period.
items.because: The basis for the 68% reduction is unclear.

items.says: Give more context for “ML-extracted features.”
Label the change from 71% to 79% as an eight-percentage-point gain if that is what you mean.
Make the key contribution and result understandable without knowledge of the training setup.
items.because: The methods are technically dense.

items.says: Explain how dynamic batching affected single-request inference latency.
items.because: Readers may wonder how batching affected a single request.

items.says: State the workload and measurement conditions.
Clarify whether the 40% change measures latency, throughput, or something else.
The bullet is grammatically incomplete and has no clear subject.
items.because: It starts with a method description.

items.says: Distinguish this latency result from the previous one.
items.because: The two bullets overlap.

items.says: Identify the measured baseline.
Focus on the result rather than the list of techniques.
Expand specialized acronyms if the target audience may not know them.
Explain what improved when training stabilized.
items.because: A measurable result or practical consequence would make the impact clear.

items.says: Explain why you used a single rollout per prompt and what effect it had.
items.because: The choice may invite questions from technical reviewers.

items.says: “Stabilised” uses British spelling.
items.because: The résumé otherwise reads as US English.

items.says: Clarify your role in creating the abstention rules and escalation paths.
Say whether the runbook meaningfully changed reviewer practice or operations.
items.because: The impact should remain modest and precise if there is no further evidence.

items.says: Replace the vague project role “Owner” with a clear responsibility.
Check when the project began and whether it is still active.
items.because: The listed dates should accurately reflect both.

items.says: Replace or remove the broad, unsupported impact claim.
items.because: A specific practice and demonstrable result would substantiate it.

items.says: The stated 50% reduction is incorrect; 900 ms to 600 ms is a 33.3% reduction.
items.because: The percentage does not match the figures.

items.says: Explain how latency was measured and under what workload.
The 71%-to-83% change is a 12-percentage-point increase, not a 12% relative increase.
items.because: The metric is labeled inaccurately.

items.says: Add benchmark context.
items.because: The result needs to be interpretable.

items.says: Clarify your authorship or contribution to the eight metrics.
Ensure “default benchmark for every release” is precise and still true.
Explain what the correlation was compared against.
items.because: “Tracks injected degradation” is broad, so the correlation’s meaning is unclear.

items.says: Describe how the degradation trials were set up and check the 400+ count.
items.because: The trials should be counted and described consistently.

items.says: Make “structural pipeline defects” and “layered instrumentation” more specific.
items.because: They are vague to readers outside the project.

items.says: Distinguish defects you found, changes you made, and fixes made by others.
items.because: Your contribution is unclear.

items.says: Add downstream impact if you can support it.
Git does not fit under “Programming” as a language.
items.because: Git is a tool, not a programming language.

items.says: Keep the skills list focused on the roles you are targeting.
Kubernetes is grouped as an ML or agent technique.
items.because: It is infrastructure.

items.says: Make broad entries such as “agent evaluation” more specific.
Use consistent date, location, punctuation, and spelling conventions throughout.
Check the final PDF for awkward line breaks, especially split “on-call” text.
